tldr: This paper gives a two-level correction for causal quantile treatment effect inference. First, original-row independent-uniform gradient perturbations with separately refitted nuisances have the observable generic covariance frontier \(K_0^{\omega}-K_U^{\omega}=-K_C^{\omega}\), retaining both outcome--nuisance cross terms. For the Sun likelihood stack the fitted estimator has kernel \(K_0-\Pi\) and the perturbation has \(K_U+\Pi\); known probabilities and frozen estimated weights are separate experiments. Legal fitted causal laws belong to the anchor's published class and refute its unrestricted Theorem 3, including actual shared-curve and separately-redrawn-rank undercoverage. Second, arbitrary smooth probability maps with locally nonsingular information can have global aliases: exact uniform data-only conditional-law estimation is impossible in general, and ordinary score multipliers and pairs resampling can fail even at a fixed alias law. Observable probability-map geometry supplies a computable sufficient injectivity test restoring uniform root-\(n\) honest bands, together with exact pointwise finite-grid validity tests at finitely many regular aliases. The generic covariance frontier, published-procedure failures and smooth alias/geometry frontier are the mathematical contributions. The shared-record joint-score band on \(\mathcal M\), and its smooth-map geometry extension, use established Gaussian tools. No numerical Kaiser reanalysis is claimed.
gap: QTE resampling validity depends on the covariance that a particular procedure preserves. Existing assignment-dependence diagnostics do not classify independent rank replacement on original rows together with separately resampled nuisance equations.
